method_note: Every number below is `python3 tools/probes.py <probe> <png>` on the checked-in shot directories. I added no probe, changed no probe, bumped nothing. `tintlaw` (the size-to-tint probe the brief asks for) already existed at v7 and measures exactly what was asked, so I did not hand-roll one. Where the frozen instrument is too noisy to carry a claim I say so and drop the claim rather than convert it into a delta.
biggestGap: An individual droplet is still an opaque, flat-filled smooth lozenge with one stamped specular pip and no optical interior — 60.22% of the hero's off-body blobs now fit a perfect ellipse at IoU>=0.90, against plate-01's own 32.47% on the same frozen probe, and that number went the WRONG way this round (r6 38.60%).

TASK_1_LIQUID_PHASE_GENUINELY_FIXED.noise_floor_I_VERIFIED_MYSELF: The builder claims the harness is non-deterministic. I checked it on the frozen probe against its own same-code pair: droplets on 02-cut+33ms reads 191 px / 3 blobs (shots/r7-juice-base) and 186 px / 3 blobs (shots/r7-juice-base2) — 2.6% mass, 0 blobs. So the +33 ms movement is 2.6x-4.5x mass and 3x-5x blob count against a 2.6% floor. It is real and it is the largest clean movement in this round.
TASK_1_LIQUID_PHASE_GENUINELY_FIXED.eye: shots/r7/02-cut+33ms.png vs shots/r6/02-cut+33ms.png is not a close call. r6 is four thin red spikes on a bare melon. r7 has a connected translucent fan with radial tears reaching ~1 fruit-radius past the silhouette. R2's film beat now exists.
TASK_1_LIQUID_PHASE_GENUINELY_FIXED.caveat_the_r6_verdict_asked_for: The r6 fix note asked whether the film was absent or merely fused into the body component. Answer: BOTH probes subtract `largest_component(L > 0.06)`, so a film still clinging to the cut face is counted as body and is invisible to droplets/particles/tintlaw by construction. That is why r7 also had to push `reach` past the silhouette. The probe cannot score a film; it can only score the part that has left the fruit. Nobody should chase this metric past the point where the sheet is physically plausible.

TASK_2_SIZE_TO_TINT_NO_LONGER_BACKWARDS.probe: tintlaw (frozen). sat_size_slope = sat_large - sat_small; POSITIVE is the REFERENCE_BAR R1b law.

15-fast-flick+50ms.read: SIGN FLIPPED, on the largest small-blob sample in the set. sat_blob_mean 0.1031 — the fast aerosol is genuinely achromatic. This is the plate-02 requirement and it is met.

00-hero.read: 5x closer to zero on the biggest samples in the project; still not positive.

TASK_2_SIZE_TO_TINT_NO_LONGER_BACKWARDS.the_frame_I_REFUSE_to_score: 16-slow-cleave+50ms reads -0.1348 (r6) -> -0.1367 (r7) and looks unmoved. It is not measurable. Two runs of IDENTICAL r6 code give slope -0.1954 (r7-juice-base) and -0.0688 (r7-juice-base2) with n_small 8 and 3. The run-to-run swing on that frame is 0.127, i.e. ~65x the apparent r6->r7 delta. I verified this myself on the frozen probe. Calling that frame 'not fixed' would be exactly the wrongly-harsh error the brief warns about, so I am not calling it anything.
TASK_2_SIZE_TO_TINT_NO_LONGER_BACKWARDS.reference_anchor: For scale: plate-01 itself reads sat_size_slope -0.0259 on tintlaw, and plate-02 reads -0.3586 on 6 blobs. The slope is not a metric that saturates at a known target; the population statistic that matters is sat_small, and r7's fast-flick sat_small of 0.1213 is the honest pass.
TASK_2_SIZE_TO_TINT_NO_LONGER_BACKWARDS.verdict_on_task_2: The law ran backwards on all five measured frames in r6. In r7 it is positive on three of them with usable samples and flat on the hero. Substantially fixed. It is no longer the biggest gap.

particles.median_blob_area.read: the split had actually COLLAPSED to 1.0x in r6 on this statistic; it is back.

TASK_3_FAST_SLOW_SIZE_SPLIT_HELD.read: The split holds on all four frozen statistics, 1.9x-3.4x, and is stronger than r6 on two of them. The brief's '4.0 vs 15.5' is not reproducible on any frame in either directory — 15.5 is r7's droplets median_area_px on the FAST frame, not a slow one. Confirmed held; the specific pair of numbers in the brief was mis-transcribed.
TASK_3_FAST_SLOW_SIZE_SPLIT_HELD.heavy_tail_BONUS: droplets.area_p95_over_median on 00-hero: r6 6.95 -> r7 8.58, against plate-01's own 8.84. The R1b 'heavy-tailed, biased hard toward small' requirement is now essentially matched. This was not asked for and it moved.

THE_REGRESSION_and_why_it_is_now_the_hea.mechanism_confirmed_by_arithmetic: fluid.js's own measurements (lines ~734-776) record that a single star-convex drop fits an ellipse at IoU>=0.90 ~99% of the time and a union-of-two-discs doublet ~10%. Line 1668 sets `dblRim = 0.45, dblSpray = 0.35`. Mixing those: 0.55*0.99 + 0.45*0.10 = 0.59. Measured: 0.6022. The model predicts the observed number to within 2 points, so the cause is not in doubt: ~60% of resolvable drops are still the single smooth outline, and r7's Beer-Lambert brightening (the dark-core floor going 0.11 -> 0.26 at line 925) lifted each one's whole smooth skirt above the probe's 0.06 luma floor where before only its irregular core survived. r7 made the drops better-lit and in doing so exposed that they are all the same shape.
THE_REGRESSION_and_why_it_is_now_the_hea.eye_at_1_1: Cropped shots/r7/00-hero.png at (900,80)-(1160,340) and (300,380)-(560,640) and viewed at 3x. Every resolvable drop is the same object: a smooth ellipse, uniformly flat-filled in one of exactly two colours (saturated red or white), carrying one small white pip in the same relative position and orientation on each. No drop shows the background through it. No drop shows a dark refractive core with a hot caustic rim — the r7 B2 floor lift to 0.26 removed the dark centre the code comment at line 922 says plate-01 has. The defocused drops render as flat uniform discs with no edge ring, where a real defocused specular drop bokehs to a bright annulus. This is REFERENCE_BAR's 'Droplets: wildly varied in size, specular, with visible refraction/darkening at the core and a bright rim' failing on three of its four clauses; size is the one it now passes.
THE_REGRESSION_and_why_it_is_now_the_hea.why_this_and_not_the_film: The film beat moved 5x and the tint law flipped sign. Those were the two named tasks and they are done. What is left is that the atom of the whole system — one droplet — is a decal, and at 1280x720 there are ~93 of them in frame all agreeing with each other. That is the instant tell.

evidence.BLIND_TEST: Unlabelled, I pick shots/r7/00-hero.png as the render in under a second, and the thing that gives it away is the droplet field, not the fruit and not the sheet. shots/r7/15-fast-flick+50ms.png is a different story — the achromatic aerosol wedge off the cut plane is genuinely close to plate-02 and I would hesitate on a small reproduction. The piece is now bimodal: the fast frame is the best thing this project has produced, the hero is still clearly synthetic.
evidence.PORTRAIT_shots_r7-iphone: No juice-specific portrait bug found. tintlaw on r7-iphone/15-fast-flick reads sat_small 0.1665, sat_blob_mean 0.1282 (achromatic mist survives the smaller raster); 02-cut+33ms reads slope +0.6629 and droplets mask 349 px on a ~100k-px raster vs landscape's 499 px on a 230k-px raster, i.e. proportionally DENSER in portrait. 16-slow-cleave portrait slope -0.1537 is inside the same 0.127 run-to-run noise as landscape and I do not score it.

fix: src/juice/fluid.js line 1668, `const dblRim = 0.45, dblSpray = 0.35;`. Raise both to ~0.75. The file's own recorded measurements (lines 734-776) give the single-drop outline IoU>=0.90 at ~99% and the doublet at ~10%; solving f*0.99 + (1-f)*0.10 = 0.3247 for the plate-01 target gives f = 0.247, i.e. dblRim = dblSpray = 0.75. That is a two-number edit with the cost already paid — `dbl` is a CPU-side coin flip, the union-of-two-discs branch is already compiled into the same program, and DBL_AREA already compensates the quad. Predicted: droplets on 00-hero pct_iou_ge_090 60.22% -> ~32%, median_iou_to_ellipse 0.9249 -> ~0.83, both landing on plate-01's native 32.47% / 0.8228, with area_p95_over_median held at 8.58 (do not let it fall below 7.5). THEN, and only then, the interior: line 925's r7 (B2) floor lift, `mix(1.12, 0.26 + ndl*ndl*0.62, big)`, took the dark core out of the fat beads that the comment at line 922 correctly says plate-01 has. Restore a dark centre WITHOUT losing the skirt by making the floor size-dependent rather than flat — keep 0.26 for big < 0.4 (which is what saved the mid-size population's luma) and ramp it back toward 0.13 as big -> 1, and simultaneously lift the caustic at line 883 out of its `big*big*(0.10 + gain*0.45)` gate, which currently puts it below the 0.06 luma floor on all but the largest handful of drops. Do NOT touch tintlaw's fast-flick numbers (sat_small must stay <= 0.14) and do NOT chase 16-slow-cleave's sat_size_slope — I have shown it swings 0.127 between two runs of identical code and it cannot be used as a target.
